title: Annotatio VI §.I: Reformed allow extrinsic sense for Indigni; Lutherans claim intrinsic too
pass_a_gloss: As in the latter sense the Reformed do not deny even to the Unworthy Sacramental and Oral Eating of Christ’s body, so the Lutherans maintain that to the Unworthy also in the former sense Sacramental Eating of Christ’s body — i.e. Oral — belongs. But of which Unworthy each side speaks must next be examined, the Apostle supplying the handle of inquiry when at 1 Cor. 11:27 he professes that some eat Christ’s body unworthily.
pass_b_english: Reformed deny the unworthy neither sacramental nor oral eating in the extrinsic sense; Lutherans hold the unworthy also have the intrinsic (true Oral) sense.
Next: which unworthy each side means — the Apostle’s handle is 1 Cor. 11:27, some eating the body unworthily.
source_text: Uti posteriori sensu Manducationem corporis Christi Sacramentalem Oralémque ne Indignis quidem abnuunt Reformati, ita Lutherani Indignis priori quoque sensu, Manducationem corporis Christi Sacramentalem, i. e. Oralem, competere sustinent. De quibus autem Indignis loquatur utraque pars, id proximè dispicendum, ansam disquisitionis suppeditante Apostolô, quando 1. Cor. 11, 27. quosdam indignè corpus Christi manducare profitetur.
